title: When Deepfake Detection Meets Graph Neural Network: a Unified and Lightweight Framework

problem.claim: Detecting AI-generated and manipulated videos is an urgent challenge.

gap.claim: Existing approaches often generalize poorly across manipulation types because they rely on isolated information modalities and typically require large models.

contributions.claim: SSTGNN represents videos as structured graphs for joint reasoning over spatial inconsistencies, temporal artifacts, and spectral distortions.
The framework combines learnable spectral filters with spatial-temporal differential modeling in a unified graph-based architecture.
SSTGNN is designed as a lightweight framework for resource-friendly real-world deployment.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on diverse benchmark datasets are reported to show superior performance in in-domain and cross-domain settings.
The framework is reported to offer strong efficiency and resource allocation.
SSTGNN is reported to use up to 42× fewer parameters than state-of-the-art models.

narrative_sequence.summary: AI-generated and manipulated videos create an urgent detection challenge.
Existing methods struggle with cross-manipulation generalization and often depend on large models.
SSTGNN models videos as structured graphs for joint spatial, temporal, and spectral reasoning.
Learnable spectral filters and spatial-temporal differential modeling are integrated into the graph architecture.
Benchmark experiments are reported to show strong performance and efficiency, including up to 42× fewer parameters.

source_observation.claim: The framework jointly models spatial, temporal, and spectral information using a structured graph representation.

interpretation.claim: Combining complementary information modalities may address failure modes caused by isolated feature reasoning.

application.claim: Use unified multimodal graph modeling when a task depends on interacting spatial, temporal, and spectral signals.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the reported deepfake detection setting.

source_observation.claim: The reported performance is achieved with up to 42× fewer parameters than state-of-the-art models.

interpretation.claim: Reducing model size can support deployment in resource-constrained environments while retaining reported effectiveness.

application.claim: Prioritize parameter efficiency when deploying video detection systems in real-world resource-constrained settings.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the deployment hardware, latency, energy use, or operational constraints.
